config.prompt: Match each situation to the kind of graph that models it.

left.label: Walkways you can walk both ways

right.label: Undirected graph: each edge goes both ways
Directed graph: each edge goes one way

solution.explanation: Correct. When a link works both ways, the graph is undirected. When it works one way only, the graph is directed.

feedback.s1: Not quite. You can walk a walkway both ways, so its edge has no direction. Ask: does the link work both ways?
feedback.s2: Not quite. A one-way street can only be driven one way, so its edge needs an arrow. Ask: does the link work both ways?
feedback.s3: Not quite. If Ama is Ben's friend, Ben is also Ama's friend, so the edge goes both ways. Ask: does the link work both ways?
feedback.s4: Not quite. You can follow someone who doesn't follow you back, so the edge goes one way. Ask: does the link work both ways?

hints.body: For each situation, ask: does the link work both ways?
An edge that works both ways is undirected. An edge that works one way only is directed.
Walkways and friendships work both ways. A right item can fit more than one situation.
Answer: walkways → undirected; one-way streets → directed; friends → undirected; following on Instagram → directed.
